newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share rally ebbs, but outlook seen good.
newsitem.headline: German share rally ebbs, but outlook seen good.

text.p: German shares extended Monday's dramatic gains to surge to fresh records in early trade on Tuesday, shrugging off a wobbly start by Bunds and cheered on by some well-received corporate earnings.
Although the rally ebbed in the first hour of trading, many dealers said the market appeared healthy and ripe for more gains in the short term.
The IBIS DAX index was up 2.03 points at 3,671.34 points at 0734 GMT, some 20 points off a new all-time high of 3,691.56 points early in the session.
"We need calm after the past two days," a dealer said.
"This is a healthy sign in a market," he added.
The early push looked like sending the IBIS DAX over a key psychological threshold of 3,700 points for the first time ever, but the impetus flagged.
"We may not see 3,700 today but that it not the end of it," said a Stuttgart dealer. "I am confident we can make it there."
The outperformers of the day were steel group Thyssen AG and retailer Metro AG, both of which released better-than-expected profit figures in the morning.
Metro rose 3.8 percent to 184.30 marks after reporting its first group profit on ordinary activities of 1.1 billion marks.
Thyssen hit a high of 404 marks before settling back to trade up 7.50 marks, or 1.9 percent, at 401 marks after it reported an 81 percent rise in first half pre-tax profit.
"Those were excellent numbers, not only from Thyssen but also from Metro," said a dealer.
"That was a real surprise and an added boost for the market in the morning."
Some dealers said they had been wrong footed by the gain in prices in early trade and expected to see a weaker trend prevailing through the day.
"This is no day for records," one Frankfurt dealer said.
The fact that Bunds were weak argued against more gains for shares, the dealer added.

Moreover he said Monday's rally was largely due to a reweighting of institutional portfolios in favour of Germany and out of France after the surprising left wing victory in the first round of parliamentary elections.
